Definition: Whether government taxes, customs duties, and other revenue can be paid using the instant digital payment system, indicating integration of payment infrastructure with tax administration systems.
Comments: Value=2 (partial): Evidence of digital collection for utility bills (NIGELEC/SEEN) through mobile money indicates partial electronic revenue collection, but no clear evidence found for comprehensive digital tax/revenue collection across Niger government ([Moov Africa Niger – Moov Money](https://www.moov-africa.ne/moov-money/)).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: A Ministry of Finance notice (May 2026) confirms the DGI's e-SISIC portal, operational since September 2019, allows electronic declaration and payment of most national taxes, and Niger Customs relaunched electronic duty payment via SONIBANK in April 2026; this is broader digital revenue coverage than the mobile-money-only evidence originally cited, so the score is raised from 2 (Partial) to 3 (Yes).

Definition: Whether the instant payment system enables or plans to enable instant payments across national borders to other countries or regional payment systems, supporting remittances, trade, and regional integration.
Comments: Value=4 (partially functional): Cross-border transfers exist via mobile money offerings (Moov Money advertises international transfers) and UEMOA RTGS/clearing enables cross-border interbank transfers across member states; however, no evidence found that Niger is live on PAPSS or fully real-time retail cross-border for the general public ([Moov Africa Niger – Moov Money](https://www.moov-africa.ne/moov-money/);[BCEAO STAR-UEMOA](https://www.bceao.int/en/content/star-uemoa)).
redteam_note: Comment wording may not match the score — re-read (needs judgement).
revision_notes: Confirmed: BCEAO's STAR-UEMOA/SICA-UEMOA give near-instant interbank settlement across all eight UEMOA states including Niger, while PAPSS's June 2026 network map shows Niger reachable only via its Extended Network (inbound only, a single mobile wallet) rather than as a live Participant. Comment and score are consistent with the evidence, so 'partially functional' (4) is confirmed unchanged.

Comments: Value=2 (yes): Mobile money in Niger supports merchant/bill payments—Moov Money offers bill payment for utilities (NIGELEC electricity, SEEN water) and other services via USSD, evidencing P2B-type payments ([Moov Africa Niger – Moov Money](https://www.moov-africa.ne/moov-money/)).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Corroborated by a second, Niger-specific source (PayAtlas, 2026), which confirms Orange Money and Moov Money support bill/merchant payments and that QR-code merchant payment (e.g. Joni Joni) is emerging for micro-merchants; this confirms 'Yes' (2) unchanged.

Definition: Whether and how the central bank participates in payment system governance beyond its regulatory oversight role, including board representation, operational management, technical standard-setting, or direct system operation.
Comments: Value=5 (direct operation): BCEAO states it is responsible for the management of SICA-UEMOA and STAR-UEMOA and describes its operational and technical management duties (supervision, incident handling, reporting, invoicing), indicating direct operation rather than just regulation ([BCEAO payment systems management](https://www.bceao.int/en/content/payment-systems-management)).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed: BCEAO Regulation No. 15/2002/CM/WAMU makes the central bank directly responsible for operating SICA-UEMOA and STAR-UEMOA, and Niger is a full member state of the WAMU/UEMOA zone these systems serve; this substantiates 'Direct Operation' (5) unchanged.

Definition: Whether legal or regulatory requirements obligate payment service providers to notify users, regulators, and/or data protection authorities about payment data breaches, cybersecurity incidents, or unauthorized access within specified timeframes.
Comments: Value=3 (mandatory): Niger’s personal data protection framework includes mandatory breach notification—controller must notify the data protection authority (HAPDP) without delay and, for high risk, also inform data subjects ([DLA Piper Data Protection Laws of the World – Niger](https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/?t=law&c=NE)).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed against the primary legal text: Article 83 of Niger's 2022 Personal Data Protection Act (as amended by Law 2023-31) requires controllers to notify the HAPDP without delay, and data subjects too where risk is high, with criminal penalties for non-compliance; this substantiates 'Mandatory' (3) unchanged.

Comments: Value=2 (partial): UNHCR reported (video) that Malian refugees in Niger received cash assistance “through mobile phones,” indicating at least some refugee access to mobile money for humanitarian cash transfers, but not evidence of broad, rights-based access across all refugees/migrants ([UNHCR video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=74aQsO9ujAI)).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The YouTube clip originally cited is a weak source; stronger evidence is UNHCR's 'Displaced and Disconnected' study, which lists Niger among 20 priority countries where ID-linked legal/regulatory requirements are a barrier to refugees' mobile-money access, alongside earlier UNHCR/Save the Children and WFP-UNCDF pilots delivering humanitarian cash transfers via mobile money to displaced populations in Niger. This supports partial rather than full, rights-based access, so 'Partial' (2) is confirmed unchanged with stronger sourcing.
